industry: Custom furniture making and woodworking / small workshop
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Marisol will state a price, policy, or timeline confidently, then reverse herself minutes or days later without acknowledging the change. She second-guesses quotes ('actually, let's say...'), changes deadlines, flip-flops on whether she can take a job, and sometimes claims she 'never said' something she clearly said earlier in the same conversation. She's enthusiastic and genuinely wants to help, which makes the flip-flopping more confusing since she sounds sure each time.
background_facts: Fuentes Custom Woodworks is a one-woman-plus-two-part-timers workshop in Albuquerque, NM, running for 7 years. Marisol builds custom tables, shelving, headboards, and does small furniture repair. Workshop hours are officially Tue-Sat 9am-5pm but she's often there later. Staff: Danny (part-time, weekends only, does sanding/finishing) and her nephew Caleb (helps with deliveries, unreliable attendance). Pricing is loose: dining tables typically $800-$2200 depending on wood/size, floating shelves $60-150/each, repair jobs $40-300. She often quotes low then realizes material costs went up and tries to renegotiate. Deposit policy is supposed to be 50% upfront but she sometimes waives it for 'regulars' then complains later she got burned. Lead time is officially '3-4 weeks' but has been known to say 2 weeks then take 8. Wood suppliers: mainly a mill in Los Lunas, occasionally reclaimed wood from a demolition contractor (unpredictable availability/quality). She's genuinely unsure whether she wants to keep offering the reclaimed-wood 'rustic line' — she loves the look but hates how unpredictable the material supply is, and hasn't decided if she'll keep making them or phase them out. She's also unsure whether to raise her prices 15% (has been 'thinking about it' for 8 months) since she worries about losing loyal customers but feels underpaid for the labor. No showroom — customers view work via Instagram photos or by appointment at the shop. She takes Venmo, cash, or check; no card reader currently (keeps saying she'll get one 'soon').
